content: Crunchbase News https://news.crunchbase.com/ Data-driven reporting on private markets, startups, founders, and investors Fri, 13 Nov 2026 20:50:40 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=6.8.12 https://news.crunchbase.com/wp-content/uploads/cb_news_favicon-150x150.png Crunchbase News https://news.crunchbase.com/ 32 32 VC Firm Plural Closes On $1.1B To Invest In European Startups With Potential For ‘GDP-Level Impact’ https://news.crunchbase.com/venture/plural-closes-billion-euro-fund-european-ai-robotics-defense-startup-investment/ Mon, 16 Nov 2026 07:00:39 +0000 https://news.crunchbase.com/?p=94388 Early-stage startup investor Plural says it has closed on its largest fund to date — just over $1.1 billion, or 1 billion euros — to lead early-stage investments across Europe. With the announcement, Plural joins a select group of European venture firms that have raised funds of a billion dollars or more in recent years. Others include Balderton Capital , Atomico and Index Ventures , which is co-headquartered in London and San Francisco. It also follows a Q3 that marked Europe’s strongest venture funding quarter in years . “Our common theme is ambition. We go after the founders that are building the most ambitious things we can humanly find,” Sten Tamkivi , a co-founder of the firm, said in an interview with Crunchbase News. “Our stated objective remains to have a GDP-level impact on Europe with the companies that we back.” Plural partners from left: Ian Hogarth, Taavet Hinrikus, Khaled Helioui, Carina Namih, Sten Tamkivi and Pierre-Dimitri Gore-Coty. (Courtesy photo) Plural’s portfolio is a mix of energy, compute, defense, robotics, health and software. The firm first backed fusion energy company Proxima Fusion in its 2023 pre-seed round and has also invested in energy storage company Ore Energy . In defense and aerospace, its investments include European defense tech company Helsing and hypersonic flight and missile company Hypersonica , whose Series A it led in 2026. Plural also led the 2024 Series B for The Exploration Co. , which develops space transportation. In robotics and manufacturing, Plural has backed Monumental , which develops bricklaying robots; Sunrise Robotics , which builds robots for manufacturing; CircuitHub , which manufactures circuit board assemblies; and Upside Robotics , which develops agricultural robots. In compute, its investments include optical AI accelerator company Olix and photonic networking company Oriole Networks . More recently, Plural led the pre-seed round for Callosum , which is building a routing layer for heterogeneous compute. Its investments have shifted year to year and fund to fund based on where the most ambitious founders are pulling the firm, said Tamkivi. “Europe has agonized maybe a little bit too much about, ‘Hey, we missed this wave in the models, and the big labs are in the U.S. and China,’ and so forth. But if you look at the rest of the pyramid, we’re doing well,” he said. The latest fund is the firm’s third and is double the size of its fund 2, raised in 2024, and 4x its first fund, closed in 2022. Plural’s portfolio companies have had a breakout year, raising more than $3 billion in follow-on capital so far in 2026. The team has six equal partners, all prior founders and operators based in London, Tallinn and Paris. Plural was founded by Taavet Hinrikus , co-founder of Wise , and Tamkivi co-founder of Teleport , both early employees at Skype , as well as Ian Hogarth , co-founder of Songkick , and Khaled Helioui , former CEO of Bigpoint . The team has two other partners: Carina Namih , co-founder of HelixNano , and Pierre-Dimitri Gore-Coty , a former Uber executive. Each partner aims to make one to three new investments per year, leaving bandwidth to work hands-on with founders. The firm’s entry point is seed and Series A, where it likes to lead. “We’re still early-stage investors, so two-thirds of this money that we raise goes into early stage. What’s Next After Huang? https://news.crunchbase.com/venture/huang-nvda-ai-startup-funding-record-2026/ Fri, 13 Nov 2026 20:32:55 +0000 https://news.crunchbase.com/?p=94391 Before it was thrust into crisis this week, Nvidia was steadily continuing its pace as one of the busiest startup investors around, including backing many of the biggest venture deals of 2026. The chipmaker and its NVentures arm have participated in more than 120 startup funding deals so far this year, according to Crunchbase data , already topping last year’s record-setting pace and marking its most prolific year yet as a private-company investor. With co-founder Jensen Huang ’s sudden departure this week amid reports of multiple extramarital affairs including with employees and a woman U.S. intelligence experts suspect of spying for China , we took a fresh look at where Nvidia and NVentures have been investing and what the future could hold. A widening investment footprint Nvidia is the most active corporate investor so far in 2026, an analysis of Crunchbase data shows. It and NVentures together are also among the top 20 most active investors in startups this year overall. Nvidia’s startup investments this year total 121 and span AI model developers, data center operators, robotics startups and healthcare companies. That continues the broad approach we examined last year , when the company and its venture arm participated in 91 known startup financings, up from 54 the year prior. The largest Nvidia-backed deals in 2026 include OpenAI ’s Series G, which closed at $122 billion in March, and Anthropic ’s $30 billion Series G in February. (Those figures represent the entire rounds, including other investors’ contributions, rather than Nvidia’s individual checks.) The company also participated in a $3.9 billion September Series F for AI infrastructure provider Crusoe and a roughly $3.5 billion September Series D for model developer Mistral AI . Of course, large as those deals are, Nvidia’s startup bets represent a small fraction of the company’s incredible market capitalization. Even as its share price tumbled this week with Huang’s departure and the surrounding news, Nvidia’s valuation remains close to $4 trillion. Beyond the biggest AI labs NVentures’ activity shows how far that investment footprint extends beyond the best-known model developers. The venture arm’s larger bets this year include robot intelligence developer Skild AI ’s $1.4 billion January Series C, and autonomous driving startup Waabi ’s $750 million Series C in the same month. It also backed two rounds for Bedrock Robotics , which develops technology to automate construction equipment: a $270 million Series B in February and a $600 million Series C in October. Its healthcare investments included a $150 million April Series E for medical imaging AI company Aidoc . As in years past, Nvidia and NVentures usually participate alongside other investors. The company or its venture arm are listed as lead or co-lead investors in about 1 in 5 of its deals this year, per Crunchbase data. For startups, Nvidia’s value as an investor also extends beyond its deep pockets. NVentures describes its offering as access to technical teams, technology integrations and help reaching customers. The question of what comes next Nvidia’s new leadership could bring a different approach to risk.
